Center tangency is \(H=\alpha u+\beta v+O(2)\), where \(\beta=b/d\) and \(\alpha=(cd-ab)/d^2\), verified by the linear invariance equation rather than quasi-stationarity. Under \(v=-r^2\), \(u=r^3q\), and \(ds/dt=r\), the two boundary saddles at \(q=\pm\sqrt{2b/(3ad)}\) are hyperbolic, supplying the incoming/outgoing curves by the stable-manifold theorem. Along the incoming curve \(tr\to2/(aQ)\), yielding all three displayed coefficients. value.rationale: The codimension-one collision \(ad=bc\) is forced by the published model’s two natural nonzero equilibrium branches; it is not an arbitrary slice. At the collision the linearized spectrum alone is dynamically inconclusive. The finding resolves a genuinely nonlinear nilpotent boundary, exhibits distinct forward/backward separatrices, and derives universal model-parameter-only slow relaxation powers and amplitudes. These clarify long transients in a nominally dissipative system and provide an exact benchmark for computations near the collision. This is not a renaming or routine spectral corollary.
